headline: EPS beat ($0.67 vs $0.40) but Capri cuts FY27 revenue to ~$3.4B on MK inventory delays, weak EMEA and FX; EPS view held.
guidance_note: FY27 revenue cut to ~$3.4B from ~$3.525B (consensus ~$3.51B); EPS ~ $2.15 held via ~$70M opex cuts; Q2 revenue ~ $780M.
key_messages: Michael Kors revenue -7.1% (-7.6% cc) to $590M; Americas -10%, a sequential improvement helped by early wholesale shipments.
MK gross margin 63.9% vs 61.1% on higher full-price sell-throughs and lower tariff rates.
Revenue cut reflects ~ $50M MK inventory delays, ~ $50M weaker EMEA (incl. Middle East), ~ $35M FX.

consumer.big_ticket: MK sales still falling as promotions and markdown inventory are reduced; Jimmy Choo growing.
consumer.pricing: Less promotional activity; lower tariff rates versus a year earlier helped margins.

macro_read: Capri's US decline is mostly self-inflicted (less discounting, supply delays), so it says more about the brand than about a weakening US consumer.
notes: Growth is as reported; Capri gives no constant-currency figure for the Americas. Versace was sold to Prada in December 2025; Jimmy Choo is still part of Capri.
Continuing operations exclude Versace (sold to Prada, Dec 2025); Jimmy Choo still included.
Company-wide gross margin change not confirmed (one source cites +200 bps, MK alone was +280 bps), so null.
Stock -4.4% (to $16.30) from a single source; revenue consensus $752.6M from a single source.
